# Shadow Strike (delivery model)

- **Status:** 🔶 Partial
- **Skills affected:** Thunder Spike
- **Mechanic tags:** shotgun, damage-pool, trigger
- **Last verified:** 2026-07-15 by Tyra
- **Backlog:** `SHADOW-01` (see `docs/INGAME_VERIFICATION_BACKLOG.md`)

## Setup

2026-07-15, RECOUNT measurement pair + ratio analysis. Character level 85, hero Erika (Lightning Shadow trait base tier 1 — source of the sheet's 18% Numbed Effect, see `thunder-spike.json`), Thunder Spike Lv20, weapon: white "Unforgotten Long Blade" only (154-154 Physical implicit, 1.5 APS, 500 crit rating), no other gear/talents. Target: Lv85 training dummy (see `training-dummy.json`). Setup A: 0 Shadow Quantity (player-hit-only baseline, N=0 shadows). Setup B: Setup A + Level 20 Haunt support (+2 Shadow Quantity → N=2 shadows, all on the same target).

## Raw data points

Setup A (N=0, solo): Recount Average DPS 349 (2:17 span), Highest-5s 410, Average-5s 320. Numbed: flat 1 stack (Thunder Spike's own inherent on-hit application; no shadows present to add more).

Setup B (N=2, + Haunt Lv20): Recount Average DPS 810 (2:00 span), Highest-5s 914, Average-5s 736. Numbed: alternates 1↔2 stacks, ~50% uptime on 2 (avg ≈1.5) — see `thunder-spike.json` notes for the newly-observed mechanism (the SHADOWS, not just the player's own hit, apply Thunder Spike's inherent Numbed here).

**Ratio (isolates the shadow delivery multiplier, but does NOT perfectly cancel — solo runs at 1 Numbed stack, Haunt runs at ~1.5 avg, so a small Numbed-difference component rides along): measured 810/349 ≈ 2.30–2.32 vs predicted `shadow_mult(N=2) = 1 + (1 + 0.30) = 2.30` × Haunt Lv20's own +0.8% support line = 2.3184.** Even accounting for the Numbed-uptime difference between the two runs, this is still the strongest evidence in this session for two specific claims: (1) the shadow term for the first additional shadow beyond the base hit carries roughly +30% weight (the −70% falloff, first application), and (2) the player's own hit contributes as a clean additive `1 +` term, unaffected by the shadow chain ("player-hit independence", Help DB's "Shadow damage and character damage are independent of each other"). It also supports Haunt Lv20 being correctly wired for +2 Shadow Quantity end-to-end (gear/support parsing → N=2 in the delivery formula).

**Caveat, RESOLVED by RUN C below (2026-07-15).** A flat-per-shadow model (`1 + 0.30(N−1)`) and a compounding-chain model agree at N=2 (both give the second shadow weight 0.30, since there is only one "further" shadow); they only diverge starting at a THIRD shadow (flat predicts 1:1.30:1.60 at N=1:2:3, compounding predicts 1:1.30:1.51). This session originally only had N=0 and N=2 data points, so the flat-vs-compounding falloff *shape* distinction needed an N=3 config to close — see RUN C immediately below, which supplies exactly that and closes it.

**RUN C (2026-07-15) — N=3 falloff-shape discriminator, CLOSES check 1.** Setup: Thunder Spike Lv20 + Haunt Lv20 (+2 Shadow Quantity) + a slate carrying "+1 Shadow" (no other relevant mods) → N=3 shadows, same base isolation build as Setup A/B. Recount Average DPS 917 (2:00 span), Highest-5s 1066, Average-5s 832. Ratio vs the Setup A solo baseline (349, N=0): measured 917/349 = 2.628. **FLAT model** (`shadow_mult(N=3) = 1 + (1 + 0.30·(3−1)) = 1 + 1.60 = 2.60`) × Haunt Lv20's own +0.8% support line = predicted ×2.6208 — matches measured within 0.3%. **COMPOUNDING model** (`1 + [1 + 0.30 + 0.30×0.30] = 1 + 1.39 = 2.39`) × 1.008 = predicted ×2.409 — misses measured by >8%, rejected. **This closes SHADOW-01 check 1: the same-target Shadow falloff is FLAT (each shadow beyond the first contributes a flat +30% weight, no per-shadow compounding of the −70% reduction), not a compounding chain.** Player-hit independence is correspondingly strengthened — the flat prediction (which assumes the player's own hit is a clean, unaffected additive term) now matches to within 0.3% across a third data point — but check 2 is not itself elevated to fully closed; the ratio still doesn't perfectly cancel the Numbed-stack difference between runs (see check 2 discussion above), so a dedicated same-Numbed-state isolation test would still close it fully.

**Shadow cadence / stacking-structure observations (owner testimony + observation, 2026-07-15) — answers SHADOW-01 check 6's structural question, though the clone-uptime FORMULA vs attack speed is still not modeled/confirmed:**
- **1 shadow (dummy test):** Numbed alternates 1↔2 stacks, ~66% at 1 stack / ~33% at 2 (avg ≈1.33). Owner notes the split is partially attack-speed-dependent — any engine model MUST derive the split from attack speed, not a hardcoded ratio.
- **Structure:** even with 4 clones (shadows) active, inherent on-hit Numbed never exceeds 2 total stacks. The structure is "1 sustained stack from the character's own hit + at most 1 sustained stack from the clones/shadows COLLECTIVELY" — shadows pool into a single second inflict-source group, not one stack per individual shadow hit. Stacks beyond 2 require an ADDITIONAL distinct inflict source (e.g. Numb Magnificent's own chance-to-inflict line, or a "+N Numbed stacks inflicted" gear/talent line) and can then exceed 2 up to the glossary Numbed cap of 10.
- **Damage-threshold pathway ruled out:** the training dummy's Max Life+ES pool is enormous/unknown, and master_glossary 762's own damage-threshold stacking clause ("When hitting a Numbed enemy, Lightning Damage inflicts 1 stack of Numbed for every 10% of the sum of Max Energy Shield and Life dealt") requires dealing a meaningful fraction of that pool per hit — at these damage levels against that target, this pathway is safely ruled out as the source of the observed 2-stack structure; the stacks are coming from the source-group mechanism above, not accumulated hit damage crossing the 10%-of-pool threshold.

**Rhythm-cadence discriminating test (2026-07-15, Part 2, verbal report -- no screenshots) -- REFUTES the phase-slot candidate model.** Owner used the Rhythm activation medium to force an exact, deterministic attack cadence (bypassing manual-cast timing jitter), same baseline as above (white-blade Erika, Thunder Spike Lv20, +1 shadow via a slate -> N=1 clone-shadow config). Results: **Rhythm 1.0s interval (1 attack/sec) -> permanently 2 Numbed stacks, 100% uptime** ("cannot get it to go lower"); **forced 2 attacks/sec -> still 100% uptime at 2 stacks**; **Rhythm 0.7s interval -> alternates 1-2 with a varying, phase-dependent percentage** (not a single stable fraction). This directly REFUTES the discrete cast-slot phase-race model recorded in `.wolf/memory.md` (2026-07-15, "Part B re-derivation"), which predicted a deterministic, aps-invariant mean of exactly 50% overlap at EVERY attack speed -- including its own stated sharpest/most-falsifiable test, aps=1.0, where it predicted a single stable 50% value with zero engagement-to-engagement spread. The measured 100% uptime at both 1.0 and 2.0 attacks/sec flatly contradicts that 50% prediction. The non-monotonic pattern across the three tested cadences (sustained 100% at 1.0s and 0.5s periods, beating/alternating at 0.7s) instead suggests an INTERVAL-ALIGNMENT mechanism -- cadences that divide evenly into Thunder Spike's own 1s inherent-Numbed inflict interval sustain both the character's and the shadows' stacks simultaneously, while a non-aligning cadence (0.7s) beats against it. **Model re-derivation is in progress (engine-agent analysis); the clone-uptime FORMULA remains OPEN/UNMODELED as of 2026-07-15** -- the phase-slot candidate (and any other single-fraction-per-aps candidate) must not be promoted or engine-implemented; the prior phase-slot writeup in `.wolf/memory.md` is retained for its record of the reasoning process but is REFUTED-BY-MEASUREMENT as of this test, not deleted.

**Solo (ZERO shadow sources) + Rhythm discriminating test (2026-07-15, same day, several repetitions each, verbal report) -- ALSO REFUTES the interval-alignment candidate.** Same baseline, but with NO shadow sources equipped at all (isolates the character's own True Body hit only): **Rhythm 1.0s -> permanent 2 Numbed stacks**; **Rhythm 0.5s -> permanent 2 stacks**; **Rhythm 0.7s -> 2 stacks ~33% / 1 stack ~66%**. **CONSEQUENCE:** the interval-alignment candidate recorded immediately above (today's earlier surviving candidate, which attributed the 2-stack sustain to shadow-hits aligning with the character's own 1s inflict interval) is ITSELF now REFUTED -- with zero shadows present, the character's own repeated hits alone reach 2 sustained stacks at some cadences. **This means the player's own applications stack independently** (each hit within Numbed's duration window can add its own stack, not just "1 sustained stack from the character, period" as previously assumed structurally). The **independent-stacking/window model** is the new working candidate (each source's hit, landing within the ailment's duration window, contributes its own stack, subject to the glossary-10 cap) -- re-derivation is in progress; NOT confirmed, NOT engine-implemented. The interval-alignment candidate is retained above for its record of the reasoning process but is REFUTED-BY-MEASUREMENT as of this same-day test, not deleted. **Important corollary under review:** the SHADOW-02 solo baseline's "flat 1 stack" was always an INFERENCE (visual/assumed), never itself directly measured at high time-resolution -- under the new independent-stacking model, solo MANUAL casting at ~1.5 attacks/sec (RUN A's cadence) would predict roughly 50% uptime at 2 stacks (by analogy to the Rhythm 0.7s-adjacent split above), i.e. an average ≈1.5 stacks rather than a flat 1. If so, this would help explain RUN A's unexplained solo −2.5% residual (`data/verification/thunder-spike.json`): +0.5 average stacks x ~5.9%/stack (18% Numbed Effect) ≈ +2.95%, close to closing that gap. **This is a hypothesis being checked, not a confirmed correction** -- flagged here so it isn't lost, but no status is promoted and no engine change follows from it yet.

**Despised Shadow's chance is USE-gated, not CAST-gated (owner-stated, 2026-07-15, verbal report).** The "33% chance to gain +N Shadows when using the Shadow Strike skill" line (exact quote, `_legendary_gear.json` `despised_shadow`) follows the standard USE-vs-CAST restriction -- it does NOT proc off triggered casts (e.g. Rhythm/Instruction activation-medium triggers, which are CASTs, not USEs). **CLOSED for AM-triggered slots, IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-15 (same batch):** `backend/engine/compute.py` (~1353-1364) now zeroes `shadow_chance_pct` whenever the slot is trigger-driven (`trigger_interval` or `wind_rhythm_base_cooldown` > 0 -- the same detection Demolisher already uses), leaving `max_shadow_quantity_flat` (flat grants -- Haunt, Frantic Shadow) unaffected; manual-use builds are unchanged, only AM/Rhythm-triggered slots are gated off. 3 new tests, full suite 3772/0. **This is the FIRST measured instance of the USE/CAST distinction mattering for a modeled mechanic** (same deferral class as Spell Burst's USE-vs-CAST gate, §0d, and Tangle's, §0c -- both still open).

## Derived / confirmed formula

Help DB `shadow-strike`: "Shadows deal the same amount of damage as the player, but if multiple Shadows hit the same enemy at the same time, the damage from each Shadow beyond the first one will additionally -70%." master_glossary 136 "Phantom" corroborates: "Multiple Shadows can attack the same target, and the Shadows' Shotgun Effect falloff coefficient is 70%. Shadow damage and character damage are independent of each other." Modeled as a delivery multiplier `shadow_mult = 1 + (1 + 0.30·(N−1))·(1 + Σ shadow_dmg_additional)` for N≥1 shadows (N=0 → mult 1.0, i.e. player hit only), where the `1 +` outer term is the player's own hit and the shadow term assumes all N shadows land on the SAME single target (first shadow full damage, each further shadow additionally −70% → contributes only 30%). Despised Shadow's "33% chance to gain +K Shadows when using the Shadow Strike skill" (exact quote, `_legendary_gear.json` `despised_shadow`) is folded in as a per-cast expected value: `shadow_mult = (1−p)·f(N_base) + p·f(N_base+k)`, `f(N)` as above (owner-approved EV mix, 2026-07-15). **Falloff shape CONFIRMED FLAT (not compounding) via RUN C (N=3), 2026-07-15 — see `notes`/`dataPoints`.** **USE-vs-CAST gating (owner-stated 2026-07-15, discovered via the Rhythm/AM discriminating tests):** the "when using" clause is USE-gated, not CAST-gated, so this EV mix must not apply on triggered (Rhythm/Instruction) casts. **CLOSED for AM-triggered slots (implemented 2026-07-15, same batch):** `backend/engine/compute.py` (~1353–1364) now zeroes `shadow_chance_pct` whenever the slot is trigger-driven (`trigger_interval` or `wind_rhythm_base_cooldown` > 0), leaving `max_shadow_quantity_flat` (flat grants — Haunt, Frantic Shadow) unaffected; manual-use builds are unchanged. 3 new tests, full suite 3772/0. See `dataPoints`/`notes` and `docs/BACKLOG.md` §0f.

## Notes / caveats / open questions

**Confirmed (Tyra, 2026-07-15) — the −70% same-target shadow falloff is FLAT, not compounding.** RUN C (N=3, Haunt Lv20 + a "+1 Shadow" slate) measured 917/349 = ×2.628 vs the solo (N=0) baseline; the flat model predicts ×2.6208 (0.3% off) and the compounding model predicts ×2.409 (>8% off, rejected). This closes SHADOW-01 check 1. Combined with the earlier N=0 vs N=2 (+Haunt) pair (measured ≈2.30–2.32 vs predicted 2.3184), player-hit independence is strengthened across three data points but remains only SUPPORTED, not fully closed — see check 2 (the ratio still doesn't perfectly cancel Numbed differences between runs; a dedicated same-Numbed-state isolation test would close it fully). Also supports Haunt's +2 Shadow Quantity wiring end-to-end and the "+1 Shadow" slate line resolving correctly. See `dataPoints` above for the full RUN C derivation.

**Still unverified:** Despised Shadow's per-cast EV-mix proc granularity for genuine USE-triggered casts (check 3 -- though its USE-vs-CAST scope is now owner-confirmed, see below), Multistrike/cast-multiplier inheritance for shadow hits (check 5), and everything under Explicitly NYI below (Tracking Area, Frantic Shadow's Attack Speed proc, Numb Magnificent's chance-inflict granularity, Charging Warcry per-enemy scaling). Check 1 (falloff shape) is now CONFIRMED (see above); check 4 (shadow-count cap) is now ANSWERED (owner-tested, 2026-07-15: no cap observed at tested counts — see `dataPoints`); check 6 (shadow-applied Numbed) is now answered-in-structure (source-group stacking, capped at 2 inherent stacks — see `dataPoints`), though the clone-uptime FORMULA vs attack speed remains OPEN/UNMODELED — a 2026-07-15 Rhythm-cadence discriminating test REFUTED the discrete phase-slot candidate model (see `dataPoints`); a same-day follow-up (solo, zero shadows, Rhythm-forced) ALSO REFUTED the interval-alignment candidate that briefly succeeded it — the player's own applications stack independently of shadows. The **independent-stacking/window model** is the current working candidate; re-derivation is in progress, formula still OPEN/UNMODELED (see `dataPoints`).

**Mechanic STRUCTURE now known (owner-reported/observed, 2026-07-15), FORMULA still unmodeled: Shadow hits can themselves apply Thunder Spike's inherent on-hit Numbed**, not just the player's own True Body hit — this is how the Haunt (Setup B) run reaches 2 Numbed stacks (player's flat 1 + a shadow-applied stack) while the solo run stays at a flat 1. Follow-up cadence testing (2026-07-15) establishes the STRUCTURE: inherent stacking is per-SOURCE-GROUP, not per-hit — "1 sustained stack from the character + at most 1 sustained stack from the clones/shadows collectively", capped at 2 total regardless of shadow count (observed up to 4 shadows), with the 1-shadow case alternating 1↔2 at ~66%/~33% (avg ≈1.33), attack-speed-dependent. This is answered-in-structure for SHADOW-01 check 6; the open question is the clone-stack UPTIME FORMULA vs attack speed — a test at a different attack speed is planned to calibrate it (three calibration points so far: N=1 avg ≈1.33, N=2 avg ≈1.5, N=4 stays <2, approaching the 2-stack structural cap). The damage-threshold Numbed pathway (glossary 762, 1 stack per 10% Max Life+ES) is ruled out as the source at this damage level (dummy pool too large). Filed alongside the existing shadow-hit-dependent NYI ledger below (Numb Magnificent's chance-on-shadow-hit — now with sampled stack ranges, see `dataPoints` — and Frantic Shadow's Attack Speed proc) — same blocker, needs the clone-uptime formula plus shadow-hit-count/timing modeling to unlock. Consequence for the model: the engine's flat-1-stack Numbed assumption (see `thunder-spike.json`) is only a conservative approximation when shadows are present; solo (no shadows) the flat-1 assumption is exact by this data. **CAVEAT ADDED 2026-07-15 (same day, after a solo/zero-shadow Rhythm-forced test — see `dataPoints`):** this "at most 1 sustained stack from the character alone" structural claim is now itself under review — the same-day solo test showed the character's OWN hits alone (zero shadows) can reach 2 sustained stacks at fast/aligned Rhythm cadences (1.0s, 0.5s). The "flat 1 solo" framing above was based on ordinary manual-cast cadence (~1.5 aps) and is not itself overturned at that cadence, but it is no longer safe to describe as a hard per-source cap of 1 — see the independent-stacking/window model discussion in `dataPoints`, which is the current re-derivation direction; nothing here is confirmed or promoted.

**CONFOUND — documented for future tests, EXCLUDED for the 2026-07-15 runs (owner testimony, 2026-07-15).** The hero trait equipped in both runs, Erika's "Lightning Shadow" tier 1 (`data/seasons/SS12/_hero_traits.json:2718`), CAN itself inflict Numbed independently of Thunder Spike or Shadows via its "Feline Figure" proc, triggered by movement-based Electrify stacks (1 stack per 3 m moved within 1 s, up to 3; "For every 1 stack(s) of Electrify, Feline Figure inflicts 1 stack(s) of Numbed"). **Owner confirms (2026-07-15) both RECOUNT runs were performed STATIONARY with NO Electrify buffs active (deliberately let them fall off before testing)** — so Feline Figure is EXCLUDED as the source of the Haunt run's second Numbed stack for these specific measurements; the 1↔2 alternation is correctly attributed to shadow-applied Numbed. This confound remains documented as something any FUTURE Thunder Spike / Shadow Strike test (with this trait equipped) must control for — confirm stationary / Electrify-inactive state — but SHADOW-01 check 6's isolation test no longer needs to re-litigate these two specific runs. See `data/verification/thunder-spike.json` notes for the same confound.

Shipped in the engine; two bugs fixed during implementation (see `.wolf/buglog.json`): `shadow-dmg-additional-generic-pool-leak` (`SHADOW_DMG_ADDITIONAL` had no `tags`, leaking into the generic `_HIT_ADDITIONAL_STATS` pool and buffing ALL hit damage regardless of Shadow Strike — fixed via a `_SHADOW_SCOPED_ADDITIONAL` frozenset) and `shadow-quantity-fuzzy-collision` (the new stat's display name "Shadow Chance Quantity" tied the fuzzy gear-text resolver against "Max Shadow Quantity" — renamed to "Shadow Chance Bonus Count"). Re-confirmed the pool-leak fix holds with real gear: attaching the same gear to `chain_lightning` (not a Shadow Strike skill) does NOT consume `shadow_dmg_additional`.

- **Tracking Area** entirely unmodeled: Thunder Spike's "100% of Skill Area increase/decrease also applied to Shadows' Tracking Area, up to 100%", the dedicated `+% Shadow(s) Tracking Area` stat family, Dual Kismet: Ghost Bee ("+50% Shadow Tracking Area +50% Shadow Strike Skill Area"), and Charging Warcry's "+20% Tracking Area for Shadow Strike Skills while the skill lasts". ## Implementation (engine model)

`backend/engine/offense.py::_shadow_multiplier` (kwarg `shadow=` on `calculate_offense`), folded into `_delivery` alongside cast/tangle/spell-burst/multistrike multipliers. Detection is data-driven off the "Shadow Strike" skill tag (NOT hardcoded to `thunder_spike`) in `backend/engine/compute.py::_offense_for_slot`, which reads `max_shadow_quantity_flat` plus the two chance stats (`Stat.SHADOW_CHANCE_PCT`, `Stat.SHADOW_CHANCE_QUANTITY_FLAT` — kept SEPARATE from the base count, not collapsed to an EV count, because `_shadow_multiplier` is nonlinear in N) from the slot-materialized source. Despised Shadow's two-literal-number chance line gets a bespoke `mod_parser.py` regex branch (can't use the single-value `_EXPRESSION_STAT_OVERRIDES` dict). Shadow sources wired: **Haunt** (support, +2 Shadow Quantity, slot-local), **Frantic Shadow** (legendary, Shadow Quantity +1), craft-base compound "Shadow Quantity +N +(A–B)% additional Shadow Damage" (`_craft_base_types.json` Ultimate Suffix, one glued line with no comma/"and" separator — bespoke regex in `mod_parser.py`), **Ronin talent `ronin_c6_r2`** (+1, resolves via `core_talent_resolver._strip_max_div`), and **Despised Shadow** itself (chance + "+(14–16)% additional Shadow Damage", corroded variant +(20–24)%, k=4 shadows). End-to-end gear verification (real `unresolved_texts`, Despised Shadow + Frantic Shadow both equipped): `shadow_count=1`, `shadow_chance_pct=0.33`, `shadow_chance_quantity=3.0`, `shadow_dmg_additional=0.15`, `shadow_mult=2.49155` — matches the hand-computed EV mix exactly.
